email.body1:
Hayden, saw Rilla launched Rilla Intelligence and brought on The Home Depot as a customer.

Moving upmarket like that usually means more in-market accounts than a business development team can cover before momentum cools, and that is where deals slip. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a signal play for Rilla off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Hayden, quick follow-up for Rilla.

At $70M ARR with enterprise logos landing, the pipeline target usually climbs faster than the team can cover by hand. Most teams don't know exactly how many meetings they need to book to hit it, so the gap shows up late and the quarter turns into a scramble.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I'll walk you through our pipeline model and show how many meetings Rilla needs to close that gap, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Hayden, last bit of proof for Rilla.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Rilla's reply rate likely compares to other scaling vertical-SaaS teams. Want to hop on a quick call so I can walk you through it?
